extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (people using tasks.lib and matrix.lib procedures)
extracted.subtask_short: SINGULAR tasks and matrix library use
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR library procedures covering task management (tasks.lib) and elementary linear algebra utilities (matrix.lib). It specifies usage, return values, assumptions and important notes for each procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: startTasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: startTasks(t1, t2, ...), t1, t2, ... tasks. Return: nothing. Starts the tasks t1, t2, ... and sets their states to 'started'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A task whose state is neither 'created' nor 'stopped' cannot be started. If applied to a 'stopped' task, computation is restarted from the beginning. Tasks can be started from within other tasks. A started task should not be accessed from within any task other than the one within which it was started. For each task, start is subject to internal scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: stopTask
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: stopTask(t), t task. Return: nothing. Stops t and sets its state to 'stopped'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A task whose state is not 'started' cannot be stopped. Intermediate results are discarded when a task is stopped. killTask() should be called for any no longer needed task.

rubrics_metrics.name: waitTasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: waitTasks(T, N[, timeout]), T list of tasks, N int, timeout int. Return: an ordered list of the indices of those tasks which have been successfully completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure waits for N tasks to complete. Optional timeout in ms (default 0 disables timeout). A task whose state is neither 'started' nor 'completed' cannot be waited for. The state of tasks that complete is set to 'completed'. Returned list may contain more than N entries if some finished already or several finish simultaneously; may contain fewer if timeout or errors occur. Polling is guaranteed: any task t for which 'pollTask(t);' would return 1 will have its index appear in the returned list. Results of completed tasks accessed via getResult(t).

rubrics_metrics.name: waitAllTasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: waitAllTasks(t1, t2, ...), t1, t2, ... tasks. Return: nothing. Waits for all the tasks t1, t2, ... to complete and sets their states to 'completed'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A task whose state is neither 'started' nor 'completed' cannot be waited for. Equivalent to waitTasks(list(...), size(list(...))) but returns nothing (no list of indices). Results of completed tasks accessed via getResult(t).

rubrics_metrics.name: pollTask
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: pollTask(t), t task. Return: 1 if computation of task t has successfully finished; 0 otherwise. The state of any task whose computation has successfully finished is set to 'completed'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A task whose state is neither 'started' nor 'completed' cannot be polled. pollTask() should return immediately, though receiving the result of the task may take some time. Result of completed tasks accessed via getResult(t).

rubrics_metrics.name: getCommand
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: getCommand(t), t task. Return: a string, the command of t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This command cannot be applied to tasks whose state is 'uninitialized'.

rubrics_metrics.name: getArguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: getArguments(t), t task. Return: a list, the arguments of t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This command cannot be applied to tasks whose state is 'uninitialized'.

rubrics_metrics.name: getResult
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: getResult(t), t task. Return: the result of t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This command cannot be applied to tasks whose state is not 'completed'. Use after waitTasks/waitAllTasks/pollTask indicate completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: getState
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: getState(t), t task. Return: a string, the state of t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States observed: 'created', 'started', 'completed', 'uninitialized', etc. See task lifecycle: createTask, startTasks, waitAllTasks, killTask, etc. Many related task procedures referenced in notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: compress
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: compress(A); A matrix/ideal/module/intmat/intvec. Return: same type with zero columns/generators deleted (for intvec, zero elements deleted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes zero columns/generators from the data structure. Examples show behavior with matrices, modules, intmat and intvec.

rubrics_metrics.name: concat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: concat(A1,A2,..); A1,A2,... matrices. Return: matrix — concatenation of A1,A2,... with number of rows = max(nrows(A1),nrows(A2),...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concatenates matrices horizontally into one matrix; shorter matrices are padded with zeros in printed examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: diag
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: diag(p,n); p poly, n integer OR diag(A); A matrix. Return: diag(p,n): diagonal matrix p times unit matrix of size n. diag(A): n*m x n*m diagonal matrix with entries all entries of the nxm matrix A in row order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates diagonal matrices from scalar/poly times identity or from flattening a matrix into diagonal entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: dsum
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: dsum(A1,A2,..); A1,A2,... matrices. Return: matrix, direct sum of A1,A2,...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places matrices on block-diagonal with zeros elsewhere; examples illustrate sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: flatten
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: flatten(A); A matrix. Return: ideal generated by all entries from A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Converts matrix entries into a one-line ideal (list of entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: genericmat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: genericmat(n,m[,id]); n,m integers, id=ideal. Return: nxm matrix with entries from id (default id=maxideal(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If id has fewer than n*m elements the matrix is filled with 0's. genericmat(n,m) creates the generic nxm matrix using base variables (x(1)..). Can provide an ideal to fill entries with specified elements (e.g., generic linear forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: is_complex
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: is_complex(c); c = list of size-compatible modules or matrices. Return: 1 if c[i]*c[i+1]=0 for all i (i.e., list forms a complex), 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideals are treated as 1-line matrices. If printlevel > 0, position where c is not a complex is shown. Useful to check whether a sequence of maps forms a chain complex.

rubrics_metrics.name: outer
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: outer(A,B); A,B matrices. Return: matrix, outer (tensor) product of A and B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computes Kronecker/tensor product; example shows block structure with products of entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: power
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: power(A,n); A a square matrix of type intmat or matrix, n integer >= 0. Return: intmat or matrix, the n-th power of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: for A=intmat and big n the result may be wrong because of integer overflow. Works over polynomial matrices (no division by polynomials).

rubrics_metrics.name: skewmat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: skewmat(n[,id]); n integer, id ideal. Return: skew-symmetric nxn matrix with entries from id (default id=maxideal(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If id has less than n*(n-1)/2 elements, the matrix is filled with 0's. skewmat(n) creates generic skew-symmetric matrix; can create skew matrices of generic linear forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: submat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: submat(A,r,c); A matrix, r,c intvec. Return: matrix, submatrix of A with rows specified by intvec r and columns specified by intvec c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selects arbitrary subsets of rows and columns (examples show specifying row vector and column ranges).

rubrics_metrics.name: symmat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: symmat(n[,id]); n integer, id ideal. Return: symmetric nxn matrix with entries from id (default id=maxideal(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If id has less than n*(n+1)/2 elements, the matrix is filled with 0's. symmat(n) creates the generic symmetric matrix; can construct symmetric matrices of generic linear forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: tensor
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tensor(A,B); A,B matrices. Return: matrix, tensor product of A and B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alias/related to outer; produces same Kronecker/tensor-block output as examples show.

rubrics_metrics.name: unitmat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: unitmat(n); n integer >= 0. Return: nxn unit matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Needs a base ring; diagonal entries are numbers (=1) in the base ring. Examples show multiplication by scalars and printing of identity matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: gauss_col
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: gauss_col(A[,e]); A a matrix, e any type. Return: a matrix B (if one argument) — the complete column-reduced upper-triangular normal form of A if A is constant (or as far as possible for polynomial matrices); or a list L of two matrices (if two arguments) satisfying L[1] = A * L[2] with L[1] the column-reduced form and L[2] the transformation matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies interred to A with ordering (C,dp); transformation matrix obtained via 'lift'. Should be faster than colred. Use only with exact coefficient fields (no pivoting/rounding treatment). Parameters are allowed: if entries are parameters, B is column-reduced form over rational function field. No division by polynomials for polynomial matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: gauss_row
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: gauss_row(A[,e]); A matrix, e any type. Return: a matrix B (one argument) — complete row-reduced lower-triangular normal form of A if A is constant (or as far as possible for polynomial matrices); or a list L of two matrices (two arguments) such that transpose(L[2])*A = transpose(L[1]) with L[1] the row-reduced form and L[2] the transformation matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure applies gauss_col to the transposed matrix; transformation matrix obtained by 'lift'. Should be faster than rowred. Use only with exact coefficient fields; parameters allowed (computation over rational function field).

rubrics_metrics.name: addcol
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: addcol(A,c1,p,c2); A matrix, p poly, c1, c2 positive integers. Return: matrix A modified by adding p times column c1 to column c2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-place column operation: column c2 := column c2 + p*column c1. Example shows polynomial p and resulting matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: addrow
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: addrow(A,r1,p,r2); A matrix, p poly, r1, r2 positive integers. Return: matrix A modified by adding p times row r1 to row r2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-place row operation: row r2 := row r2 + p*row r1. Example demonstrates resulting entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: multcol
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: multcol(A,c,p); A matrix, p poly, c positive integer. Return: matrix A modified by multiplying column c by p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-place scaling of specified column by polynomial/scalar p; examples show effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: multrow
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: multrow(A,r,p); A matrix, p poly, r positive integer. Return: matrix A modified by multiplying row r by p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-place scaling of specified row by polynomial/scalar p; examples show effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: permcol
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: permcol(A,c1,c2); A matrix, c1,c2 positive integers. Return: matrix A modified by permuting columns c1 and c2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Swaps two columns; example demonstrates column order change.

rubrics_metrics.name: permrow
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: permrow(A,r1,r2); A matrix, r1,r2 positive integers. Return: matrix A modified by permuting rows r1 and r2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Swaps two rows; example demonstrates row order change.

rubrics_metrics.name: rowred
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: rowred(A[,e]); A matrix, e any type. Return: a matrix B being the row-reduced form of A when called with one argument (as far as possible over polynomial ring; no division by polynomials); or a list L of two matrices such that L[1] = L[2] * A with L[1] the row-reduced form and L[2] the transformation matrix (if called with two arguments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed mainly for teaching; implements straightforward Gaussian algorithm (no standard basis). The transformation matrix is obtained via concatenating a unit matrix to A; proc gauss_row may be faster. Should only be used with exact coefficient fields (no pivoting) over polynomial ring (ordering lp or dp). Parameters allowed: if entries are parameters, computation is over rational function field. Assumes entries of A are in base field but does not verify.

rubrics_metrics.name: colred
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: colred(A[,e]); A matrix, e any type. Return: a matrix B being the column-reduced form of A when called with one argument (as far as possible over polynomial ring; no division by polynomials); or a list L of two matrices such that L[1] = A * L[2] with L[1] the column-reduced form and L[2] the transformation matrix (if called with two arguments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed for teaching; applies rowred to transposed matrix (proc gauss_col should be faster). Use only with exact coefficient fields (no pivoting) over polynomial ring (ordering lp or dp). Parameters allowed; entries as parameters leads to computation over rational function field.

rubrics_metrics.name: linear_relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: linear_relations(M); M a module whose non-zero entries are homogeneous polynomials of the same positive degree. Return: a maximal module R such that M*R is formed by zero vectors (i.e., relations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base field must be an exact field (not real or complex). It is not checked whether assumptions hold. Example shows computing relations and verifying M*REL is zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: rm_unitrow
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: rm_unitrow(A); A matrix (being col-reduced). Return: matrix obtained from A by deleting unit rows (rows with one 1 and else 0) and associated columns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes trivial unit rows and corresponding columns from a col-reduced matrix. Example demonstrates deletion of unit rows and collapse of columns.

rubrics_metrics.name: rm_unitcol
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: rm_unitcol(A); A matrix (being row-reduced). Return: matrix obtained from A by deleting unit columns (columns with one 1 and else 0) and associated rows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes trivial unit columns and corresponding rows from a row-reduced matrix. Example demonstrates deletion and resulting matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: headStand
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: headStand(M); M matrix. Return: matrix B such that B[i][j] = M[n-i+1, m-j+1], where n = nrows(M), m = ncols(M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reverses rows and columns (flip both axes). Example shows mirrored matrix output.

rubrics_metrics.name: symmetricBasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: symmetricBasis(n,k[,base_name]). Return: polynomial ring containing the ideal 'symBasis', a basis of the k-th symmetric power of an n-dim vector space. Output ring has characteristic 0 and variables named by given base string (default 'e').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a container ring and lists basis elements (symBasis). Example shows basis for 3rd symmetric power of 4-dim vector space. See also exteriorBasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: exteriorBasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: exteriorBasis(n,k[,base_name]). Return: qring, an exterior algebra containing the ideal 'extBasis', a basis of the k-th exterior power of an n-dim vector space. Output ring has characteristic 0 and variables named by base string (default 'e').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produces an exterior algebra with noncommutative relations (anti-commutation). Example shows extBasis and noncommutative relations; see also symmetricBasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: symmetricPower
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: symmetricPower(A,k); A module, k int. Return: module: the k-th symmetric power of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chosen bases and intermediate data will be shown if printlevel is large. Examples show symmetric power over commutative algebras and over exterior algebras (where sizes differ and may collapse).

rubrics_metrics.name: exteriorPower
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: exteriorPower(A,k); A module, k int. Return: module: the k-th exterior power of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chosen bases and intermediate data will be shown if printlevel is large. Last rows will be invisible if zero. Example context and ring/block settings indicated in documentation.
